query: I need to back up my home files and photos. Should I use a NAS or just pay for cloud storage?
atoms: perspective: Average home user minimizing complexity
perspective: Power user with large data volumes and technical comfort
trustworthiness: Home lab and self-hosting community
plausible_answers: Answer A (Cloud Storage Default): Use cloud storage (Backblaze, Google One, iCloud) — for most home users, the zero-maintenance automatic offsite protection at $3–12/month is vastly simpler than NAS ownership and protects against local disasters.

Answer B (NAS for Large Data): Buy a Synology NAS if you have 10TB+ of data — the one-time hardware cost beats cloud subscription costs over 5 years, and local speeds make backup and restore dramatically faster for large libraries.

Answer C (NAS Plus Cloud for 3-2-1): Combine a NAS for local backups with Backblaze B2 for offsite cloud replication — this implements the proper 3-2-1 backup strategy and is the only approach that protects against both local hardware failure and physical disaster.
